name: Direct lunar transfer
blurb: Five days to the Moon. Simple and quick, but you arrive fast and must brake hard.

name: Low-energy lunar transfer
blurb: A looping 3-month path that uses the Sun's gravity to arrive gently — less braking fuel, more time in space.
notes: Modelled on GRAIL / CAPSTONE-style ballistic lunar transfers.

name: Mars Type-I transfer — late 2028
blurb: The next good Earth–Mars alignment. About 7–8 months of cruise.
notes: Track B: replace with Trajectory Browser optimum for the 2028–29 window.

name: Mars Type-I transfer — early 2031
blurb: The following window, 26 months later: slightly lower launch energy, more time to build.

name: Direct to Jupiter
blurb: Straight there in under 3 years — but it takes enormous launch energy, so your spacecraft must be light.

name: Earth gravity assist (ΔV-EGA)
blurb: Launch gently, loop around the Sun, burn once in deep space, then slingshot past Earth to Jupiter. Half the launch energy, two extra years.
notes: C3, flyby day and time of flight mirror Juno (launch 2011-08-05, Earth flyby 2013-10-09, arrival 2016-07-04).
